blocks.text: Breakfast and transfer to the station for the train to the lost world in the mountains of Peru. Long hidden from view, Machu Picchu was brought to international attention by an American explorer in 1911; it was abandoned by the Incas for reasons still unknown. The beauty of the mountains, the depth of the canyon and the lush greenery make you feel part of a centuries-old mystery. After the guided visit, free time for photos, perhaps with a llama; then bus down to the village for lunch at a Peruvian restaurant, and return by train to Cusco.

blocks.text:
Breakfast. The Sacred Valley, cradle of the Inca civilisation, was renowned for its fertile land and mild climate, and the Incas built entire towns here, whose ruins remain: Urubamba, with the country estate of the emperor Huayna Cápac; Pisac, said to be shaped like a partridge; Ollantaytambo and its ceremonial centre; Chinchero, with a colonial church built on Inca foundations; and Moray, with its amphitheatre-like agricultural terraces.

Near Pisac, browse the market for silver, ceramics and leather; at the Awanakancha centre, meet llamas, alpacas and vicuñas and learn how their precious wool is dyed. Buffet lunch at a Peruvian restaurant and return to the hotel.
The Sacred Valley of the Incas
